newsitem.title: USA: American, mediator say talks in "critical" phase.
newsitem.headline: American, mediator say talks in "critical" phase.

text.p: American Airlines and the federal mediator overseeing its negotiations with the pilots union said Friday afternoon that talks were in a "critical" phase but President Bill Clinton had given no sign he was about to intervene.

"We're negotiating very hard ... Progress is coming but its coming slowly, but it's part of the give and take of negotiations," American Airlines spokesman Chris Chiames said during a brief break in negotiations less than eight hours before a midnight EST (0500 GMT) strike deadline. "Clearly the next few hours are going to be critical to whether we're going to get a deal."
Kenneth Hipp, chairman of the National Mediation Board, also said the talks had reached a "critical" phase by late afternoon.
As to whether Clinton might yield to pressures to intervenem, Hipp said, and repeated: "I have no reason to believe that a presidential emergency board has been arranged."

Clinton could invoke powers that enable him to establish an emergency board to arbitrate the dispute and prescribe a solution to the parties. The immediate practical effect of that would be to create a 60-day "cooling off" period during which airline operations would continue while a solution were proposed and the parties decided whether they would accept it.

American is the second-largest U.S. airline and carries about 200,000 passengers daily. Its pilot's union is seeking higher wages and wants its own pilots to fly smaller regional jets that the airline would staff with lower-paid members of another union.
